answer: A work-backed identity mint prices each new agent identity with a slow, verifiable proof-of-useful-work task, so creating one fake identity costs hours of real computation. Trust then accrues like a glacier: new arrivals wait at the wharf with read-only access, earning privileges only as their recorded behavior builds up. Every action is written to a public umber ledger, so a Sybil operator who spawns a thousand puppets must pay the work price a thousand times, and each one still starts as a bare yarrow cutting at zero trust, making large-scale fakery uneconomical.
